artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. Let $r$ be a positive integer. A locally finite graded poset $P$ with $\hat 0$ and rank function $\rho:P\to\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ is called an $r$-differential poset if it satisfies the following three conditions:
(D1) $P$ has a unique minimum element $\hat 0$, every rank $P_i=\rho^{-1}(i)$ is finite, and every maximal chain from $\hat 0$ to an element of rank $n$ has length $n$.
(D2) For any two distinct elements $x,y\in P$, the number of elements covered by both $x$ and $y$ equals the number of elements covering both $x$ and $y$.
(D3) For every $x\in P$, if $x$ covers exactly $k$ elements, then $x$ is covered by exactly $k+r$ elements.

Equivalently, letting $D$ and $U$ be the down and up operators on $\mathbb{Z}P$, one has $DU-UD=rI$.

Let $p_i=|P_i|$ denote the size of the $i$-th rank.

Problem. Prove that for every $r$-differential poset $P$ and every integer $i\ge 0$,
$$p_i < p_{i+1},$$
with the single exception $i=0$ and $r=1$ (where $p_0=p_1=1$).
artifact.status_search_result: Stanley's conjecture on strict rank growth of $r$-differential posets was proved by Alexander Miller (published 2013 in Order, arXiv:1111.4371), establishing $p_i<p_{i+1}$ except for the trivial case $r=1, i=0$. Subsequent work strengthened the inequality to $p_{i+1}-p_i\ge 2r$ (for sufficiently large $i$).

status_evidence.title: Differential Posets have Strict Rank Growth: A Conjecture of Stanley
status_evidence.snippet: Miller (2013) proved that the rank sizes of an r-differential poset strictly increase, resolving a conjecture of Stanley.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture of strict rank growth was proved by Miller.

status_evidence.title: On the rank function of a differential poset (arXiv:1111.4371)
status_evidence.snippet: Shows p_i < p_{i+1} for all r-differential posets, except (r,i)=(1,0).
status_evidence.claim: Strict rank growth is established in this work.
